summary: This article explains how sailors use wind angle, sail trim, and tacking to move a boat, even against the wind, and the basic tactics racers use to win.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Sailing: Wind-Powered Racing”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: a heavy fin under a boat that stops it tipping and helps it move forward
a rope used to control the angle of a sail
the group of people who work together to sail a boat

challengeTerms.def: a planned action used to gain an advantage in a contest
the force a moving object has that keeps it going
shaped so that air flows over it smoothly, creating little resistance or useful force

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that sailing without an engine is harder than driving a motorboat? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a sailor moves a boat toward a point upwind, and how trimming the sail helps during a race.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review keel, sheet, and crew, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use tactic, momentum, and aerodynamic in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
